newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Min Xin up on China/Taiwan shipping hopes.
newsitem.headline: Min Xin up on China/Taiwan shipping hopes.

text.p: Shares of Min Xin Holdings Ltd rose in Hong Kong on anticipation the company would benefit from economic growth in China's coastal Fujian province if direct shipping links do open between Taiwan and China, brokers said.
Shares of Min Xin rose HK$0.20 or 6.72 percent to HK$3.175 in late morning on volume of 5.20 million shares.

"The shipping links are expected to help boost the economy in Fujian in the future," said Kinson Au, senior analyst from PW Asia Brokerage. "As the company is one of the dominated player in that region (Fujian), it is expected to benefit from future economy growth in the region."
The Fujian-based company engages in infrastructural and property development, finance, banking and insurance, and is a major shareholder of Xiamen International Bank.
Analysts said it was expected that Min Xin's banking and insurance business would be boosted on growing trading activities in Fujian, the Chinese province nearest Taiwan.

On Wednesday, non-government negotiators from Taiwan and China reached an understanding to let shipping companies apply to open routes between Kaohsiung in Taiwan and Fuzhou and Xiamen in Fujian, but details of the accord remained murky.
